result.title: Create physics-based effects
result.technique: Physics2DPlugin for projectile motion (gravity + velocity + angle + friction). The demo itself is a particle/projectile launcher — not directly a button click micro-interaction. The transferable idea for Like/Save/Share is the broader GSAP "physics-based effects" toolkit: Physics2DPlugin for confetti/particle bursts on tap, plus CustomBounce + CustomEase for the tactile button rebound itself. The recommended port combines both: a CustomBounce squish-and-rebound on the button transform, layered with an optional Physics2D particle burst on tap (great for Like), and a per-button CSS-variable color flash driven by the same timeline.
result.keyMechanic: Physics2DPlugin animates `physics2D: { velocity, angle, gravity, friction }` on each tick — it integrates position from velocity/gravity rather than tweening to a fixed endpoint, which is what makes it feel "real". For the button feedback, you (a) overshoot the scale with CustomBounce.create("myBounce", { strength: 0.6, endAtStart: true, squash: 2 }) so the button squishes, snaps back, and settles, (b) flash a per-element CSS variable (--flash-color) to that button's brand color using gsap.fromTo on the variable so it's keyframed, and (c) optionally spawn N short-lived particle divs and animate each with `physics2D` for a confetti burst (Like only). All three are merged into one gsap.timeline() so the tactile feel, color flash, and burst stay in lockstep.
result.a11yNotes: - The feedback is purely additive: the React onClick still fires synchronously, so screen reader / keyboard users get identical behavior. The timeline is fire-and-forget. - Wrap the entire effect in `if (!gsap.matchMedia().reduced) { ... }` or check `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` and, when true, skip the squish/burst and just toggle `--flash-alpha` to 0.6 for 120ms via a single non-bouncy tween — color feedback remains, motion does not. - Particles get `pointer-events:none` and are removed onComplete so they never trap focus or block taps. - Use `transform-origin: 50% 60%` so the rebound visually anchors at the thumb, which reads as more "tactile" without affecting hit-target geometry. - Color choice for Like (#ff3860) and Save (#d4a24a) should be checked against the reading-view background for 3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11); the blurred glow alone is decorative, but if it's the only feedback in reduced-motion mode it must meet contrast. - Buttons keep their `:focus-visible` ring untouched — the ::after layer sits behind (z-index: -1) so it never masks the focus outline. - For the Like burst, particles are fixed-position but absolute-removed onComplete; they will not affect document flow, layout shift (CLS), or assistive-tech tree (they're empty spans).

result.title: ScrollToPlugin: Scroll to Element (GSAP official demo)
result.technique: gsap.to(window, { scrollTo: ... }) with ScrollToPlugin to smoothly animate window scroll to a target element or numeric Y coordinate. The canonical, supported way to animate window scroll position in GSAP. Direct replacement for native window.scrollTo({ behavior: 'smooth' }) but with full control over easing, duration, autoKill (interrupt-on-user-scroll), and onComplete.
result.keyMechanic: ScrollToPlugin teaches GSAP that the special `scrollTo` property on the `window` target means "animate window.scrollY (or scrollX) toward this value." You can pass: a number (pixel Y), an Element/selector ("#section1"), the string "max" (bottom of page), or an object { y, x, offsetY, offsetX, autoKill, onAutoKill }. autoKill defaults to TRUE on window — meaning if the user touches the wheel/touchpad/keyboard mid-animation, GSAP detects the manual scroll and instantly aborts the tween (no fight with the user). That autoKill default is the single most important behavior for a "restore last reading position" feature — it means the animation politely yields if the reader scrolls themselves.
result.a11yNotes:
CRITICAL — respect prefers-reduced-motion. The provided React port branches on window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and falls back to the existing instant window.scrollTo when a user has reduced motion enabled. Animating ~1s of vertical scroll is a known vestibular trigger.

autoKill: true is itself an a11y win. Keyboard users (PageDown, Space, arrow keys) and assistive-tech users who scroll mid-restore are NEVER fought by the animation — ScrollToPlugin detects the manual scroll attempt and instantly aborts the tween. This is the single most important reason to prefer ScrollToPlugin over a hand-rolled rAF tween or CSS scroll-behavior: smooth (which has no equivalent auto-abort).

For screen-reader users the visual restore is cosmetic. If the saved reading position corresponds to a known anchor (heading id, paragraph id), additionally call element.focus({ preventScroll: true }) after the tween settles so the SR cursor lands where the visual cursor is. Do not trap focus or add a pointer-events:none overlay during the tween — you don't need to, because autoKill handles user input gracefully.

Do not lower the contrast or animate the article body during the scroll — keep all motion confined to the scroll position itself. Compound motion (scroll + fade + transform) compounds vestibular load.

result.title: Smooth Flexbox Filtering with Flip (GreenSock CodePen NWRxarv)
result.technique: FLIP (First-Last-Invert-Play) reflow animation. Capture the bounding-box state of every card BEFORE the filter mutation, mutate the DOM (toggle each card's display between "inline-flex" and "none" so flexbox reflows the visible set), then call Flip.from(state, ...). Flip diffs the new positions/sizes against the snapshot, instantly inverts every visible card back to its old spot, and animates the removal of those offsets so cards slide into their new flex slots. onEnter handles items that re-entered the flow (fade+scale in), onLeave handles items that left (fade+scale out), with absolute:true holding leavers in their old slot during the tween so the surviving cards don't fight a layout shift mid-animation.
result.keyMechanic: Three-step lifecycle on every checkbox click: (1) state = Flip.getState(items) snapshots all 8 .item rects; (2) items.forEach(item => item.style.display = matches.indexOf(item) === -1 ? "none" : "inline-flex") — this is what makes flexbox re-pack the visible cards into a tight grid; (3) Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.7, scale: true, ease: "power1.inOut", stagger: 0.08, absolute: true, onEnter: els => gsap.fromTo(els,{opacity:0,scale:0},{opacity:1,scale:1,duration:1}), onLeave: els => gsap.to(els,{opacity:0,scale:0,duration:1}) }) tweens everything. absolute:true is the load-bearing option — it lifts the leaving cards to position:absolute for the duration of the flip so the staying cards can flow into their new flex positions without their tween being clobbered by the same reflow.
result.a11yNotes: prefers-reduced-motion: gate the entire Flip.from call (set duration:0 or skip the tween) when window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches — the demo doesn't do this. Focus management: the demo toggles display:none on items, which removes them from the tab order automatically (correct). For Lucifer's Diary, ensure focus doesn't get stranded on a card that's mid-fade-out — move focus back to the clicked tag button after navigation. Announce filter results to screen readers via an aria-live="polite" region ("Showing 24 of 87 stories") since the visual reflow is silent. Tag buttons in the demo are <input type="checkbox"> inside <label> — keep that semantic (or use role="button" with aria-pressed) so toggling state is announced; the current TagBar uses <Link> which announces as navigation rather than toggle — fine for SSR-driven filtering but worth knowing if you switch to client-side. While Flip is animating, the cards have position:absolute applied transiently — pointer-events on leaving cards should be disabled so a user can't click a card that's flying off-screen. Stagger of 0.08s feels lively but compounds: with 50+ visible cards the last one is 4s behind the first — cap stagger to {amount: 0.4} (total budget) rather than per-item for large grids.

tasks.title: Magnetic dock hover on card rows (StoryCard, SeriesCard, ChapterList row, ContinueCard)
tasks.useCase: Card lists react to the cursor like a Mac OS dock — the card under the pointer (and its neighbors) scale + lift toward the cursor, falling back to rest as the pointer moves away. Applied on the homepage hero card list, the /browse and /search CardGrid, the ContinueReadingRow card strip, and the chapter list rows on /series/[id].
tasks.gsapPlugin: core (gsap.quickTo + gsap.utils.mapRange) — no extra plugin required, just gsap.to with overwrite:auto and gsap.quickTo for the per-frame x/y/scale setters
tasks.demoReference: https://gsap.com/demos/ (magnetic-effect / dock-style hover pattern — uses gsap.quickTo + pointermove distance mapping)
tasks.approach: Add a single shared client hook useMagneticDock({ radius: 200, maxScale: 1.4, maxLift: 12 }) that scopes itself to a container ref, queries [data-dock-item] children, and on pointermove on the container maps each item's center-distance from the cursor through gsap.utils.mapRange(0..200, [1.4,1]) for scale and (0..200, [12,0]) for translateY. Uses gsap.quickTo per item for x/y/scale to avoid per-tween allocation. On pointerleave the hook tweens every item back to {scale:1, y:0, duration:0.45, ease:'power3.out'}. Each card component receives data-dock-item on its root anchor: SeriesCard <Link>, StoryCard <Link>, ContinueCard <Link>, and ChapterList's <Link className={styles.row}> in frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx (line 84). Because frontend/app/page.tsx is a server component exporting metadata, the home hero card list cannot host the pointermove hook directly — a new client wrapper frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx wraps the existing <SeriesCard> map in a div that mounts the hook. The hook's reduced-motion path no-ops the listener entirely. To prevent CSS hover transforms from fighting GSAP, the rule .card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); ... } at frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css lines 67-70 is removed, and the transform leg of the transition at lines 63-66 is removed (border-color transition stays). Same pass on .row:hover and the .row transition rules in ChapterList.module.css and equivalent rules in StoryCard.module.css / SeriesCard CSS. NOT in scope: /tag/[slug] (its layout doesn't share the dock container), admin lists, the search filter pills.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Add a Mac-style magnetic dock hover effect to card rows so the card under the cursor (and its near neighbors) scale up and lift toward the pointer.

## Why
Card rows on /, /browse, /search, /series/[id], and the ContinueReadingRow currently use a static CSS transform on :hover. A magnetic dock makes the entire row feel responsive to the cursor and reinforces "this is a curated catalog you can browse" — at the cost of one shared hook.

## Scope
- New hook: `frontend/lib/useMagneticDock.ts`
- New client wrapper: `frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx` (because `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component that exports `metadata` — it cannot host pointermove listeners)
- Add `data-dock-item` to the link root of: SeriesCard, StoryCard, ContinueCard, and the `<Link className={styles.row}>` chapter row at `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx:84`
- Mount the hook in: CardGrid, ContinueReadingRow, HeroCardsList, ChapterList

## Tuning numbers (DO NOT change without design review)
- `radius: 200` (px from cursor — falloff distance)
- `maxScale: 1.4` (item directly under cursor)
- `maxLift: 12` (px translateY toward viewport top)
- Falloff: linear via `gsap.utils.mapRange(0, 200, max, 1)`; clamp at >= 1
- Settle tween on pointerleave: `duration: 0.45, ease: 'power3.out'`

## CSS cleanup (REQUIRED)
The existing CSS `:hover` transforms will fight GSAP's quickTo writes. Remove these specific rules:
- `frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css`: delete `transform var(--transition-fast),` from the multi-property `transition:` block at lines 63-66; delete the `transform: translateY(-2px);` line from `.card:hover` at lines 67-70 (keep `border-color`)
- `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.module.css`: remove the transform leg of any `transition:` block on `.row` and any `:hover` rule that sets `transform`
- Same pass on `StoryCard.module.css`, `SeriesCard` styles, and `ContinueCard.module.css`

## Out of scope
- `/tag/[slug]` (separate layout, no shared dock container)
- Admin lists
- TagBar pills / search filter chips

## Reduced motion
`prefersReducedMotion()` causes the hook to bail before attaching any pointer listener — items stay at rest.

## Test plan
- [ ] Hover homepage hero cards — center card scales to 1.4, neighbors scale partially, all settle back on leave
- [ ] Hover /browse CardGrid — same dock feel
- [ ] Hover ContinueReadingRow on chapter page — same
- [ ] Hover ChapterList row on /series/[id] — same
- [ ] Toggle macOS reduce-motion — hook no-ops, no transform applied
- [ ] Keyboard-tab through cards — focus ring intact, no transform applied (pointermove only)
- [ ] Rapid pointer flick across the row — no tween stacking (overwrite:auto)
- [ ] DevTools throttle to 4x CPU — verify quickTo keeps up at 60fps
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: useMagneticDock first-line checks prefersReducedMotion() from frontend/lib/gsap.ts; on true it returns without attaching any listener and the cards stay at their CSS rest position. Because the CSS :hover transforms are removed in this PR, reduced-motion users get a strictly static row with no transform on hover (border-color hover still applies). No need to set inline transforms — the absence of the listener IS the fallback.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Removed fictitious ChapterCard.tsx from filesToChange — chapter rows live inside ChapterList.tsx at frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx and are `<Link className={styles.row}>` elements (line 84). Added new client wrapper frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx to filesToCreate because frontend/app/page.tsx is a server component exporting metadata and cannot host pointermove. Added frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css to filesToChange with exact line numbers (63-66 transform-transition; 67-70 hover transform) called out for removal. Pinned tuning numbers (radius:200px, maxScale:1.4, maxLift:12px) inside the issue body. Added an explicit out-of-scope list (/tag/[slug], admin, TagBar).

tasks.title: FLIP-based expand/collapse for admin NoteCard inside NotesPanel
tasks.useCase: Each admin NoteCard expands from a small pill to a full-height composer card. Today the panel uses a CSS max-height transition; this swaps in GSAP Flip so the expanding card morphs from its pill rect to its open rect (with siblings yielding via absolute:true), eliminating the layout pop when the textarea height is unknown.
tasks.approach: Inside NotesPanel.tsx, on the moment the active note id changes, capture Flip.getState() for every .card descendant BEFORE setState (using a useLayoutEffect+ref trick or by snapshotting in the click handler immediately before the React state update). After commit, useGSAP({ scope: panelRef, dependencies: [activeId] }) calls Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, simple: true, nested: true, onEnter: els => gsap.from(els, { autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.25 }) }). Mount strategy: ALWAYS render both branches — pill markup and expanded markup live in the same component tree gated by `expanded`, and the children persist across the toggle so Flip can match them by node identity. Stray autosaves on collapsed cards are gated by a debounce that checks `expanded` synchronously inside the autosave handler (drop the write if not expanded). The per-card `transition: transform 180ms, ... box-shadow 220ms` at NoteCard.module.css lines 18-22 is REMOVED for the `transform` leg only (keep border-color / box-shadow); GSAP owns transform via Flip + T1's dock writes. To reconcile T1's dock writes with Flip, all Flip.from tweens use `overwrite: 'auto'`. The panel-level `transition: max-height 260ms` at NotesPanel.module.css lines 28-31 is REMOVED on `.panel.hasExpanded` because Flip animates the expanded card's rect itself; the panel just resizes to fit. Reduced-motion path skips Flip.from entirely and sets `overflow: hidden` on the panel while open===false so the collapsed pills don't leak content during the synchronous swap. Register Flip in frontend/lib/gsap.ts.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Replace the CSS max-height transition on admin NoteCard expand/collapse with a GSAP Flip morph so the card transitions from its pill rect to its open rect with siblings yielding cleanly.

## Why
The current `transition: max-height 260ms` on `.panel.hasExpanded` (NotesPanel.module.css:28-31) can't smoothly handle the textarea's unknown intrinsic height; you see a pop on expand and a snap on collapse. Flip captures both rects and tweens between them.

## Approach (committed)
- **Mount strategy**: always render both pill + expanded markup inside the same component subtree (do NOT unmount on collapse). Children persist by ref so Flip can match them.
- **Autosave guard**: the textarea autosave handler checks `expanded` synchronously and drops the write if false (defends against the always-mounted collapsed branch firing autosaves).
- **CSS coordination**:
  - REMOVE the `transform` leg of the `transition:` block at `NoteCard.module.css:18-22` (keep border-color, box-shadow)
  - REMOVE `max-height 260ms ...` from the `transition:` block at `NotesPanel.module.css:28-31` on `.panel` (Flip animates the cards; the panel just resizes to fit)
  - Use `overwrite: 'auto'` on every Flip.from tween so T1's dock writes don't fight
- **Reduced motion**: skip Flip.from and instead toggle classes synchronously; set `overflow: hidden` on the panel when `open === false` so collapsed pills don't visually overflow during the swap
- **gsap.ts**: register Flip alongside existing ScrollTrigger — single `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, Flip)` call (see cross-cutting note in T4/T5)

## Files
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.module.css`
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts`

## Test plan
- [ ] /admin → open a note card — pill morphs to full-height composer
- [ ] Collapse it — full-height morphs back to pill, no max-height pop
- [ ] Open one, then click another — first collapses while second opens in one timeline
- [ ] Hover other note cards during expand — T1 dock effect doesn't fight Flip's transform
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — no animation, no overflow leak, autosave still works
- [ ] Edit textarea, collapse, expand — content preserved (proves persistent mount)
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: When prefersReducedMotion() is true, the Flip.from call is skipped entirely — the React commit synchronously swaps DOM classes/sizes. To prevent the always-mounted collapsed markup from visually leaking during the synchronous swap, `.panel:not(.hasExpanded) .card` gets `overflow: hidden`. Border-color hover stays via CSS.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Added NotesPanel.module.css to filesToChange and reconciled the panel-level `transition: max-height 260ms` (lines 28-31) with the per-card Flip — it must be removed because Flip owns the size animation. Committed to the always-render-both-branches mount strategy with an autosave guard (the alternative — useLayoutEffect-on-mount measure — was harder to reconcile with autosave). Specified that the reduced-motion path must set `overflow: hidden` on collapsed panels. Called out the NoteCard `.card transition: transform 180ms` rule (lines 18-22) and committed to removing the transform leg while keeping overwrite:'auto' on Flip + T1's dock for safety.

tasks.title: Physics-based click feedback for Like / Save / Share / QuoteShare buttons
tasks.useCase: Like / Save / Share / QuoteShare buttons feel tactile on press: a CustomBounce squish-and-rebound on the button itself, a per-button color flash via box-shadow, and (Like only) a Physics2DPlugin confetti burst spawning short-lived particle spans. All three layers run on one timeline.
tasks.gsapPlugin: Physics2DPlugin + CustomBounce + CustomEase (all in GSAP free tier as of GSAP 3.13+; verify isPaidPlugin:false at time of implementation)
tasks.approach: Create one shared helper `pressFeedback(el: HTMLElement, flashColor: string, burst: boolean): gsap.core.Timeline` in frontend/lib/pressFeedback.ts. It (a) tweens scale 0.86→1 with CustomBounce.create('btnBounce', { strength:0.55, squash:1.4 }), (b) flashes a box-shadow directly via gsap.fromTo(el, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 0 ${flashColor}` }, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 12px ${flashColor}00`, duration: 0.55 }) — chose direct box-shadow over CSS variables so no @property registration is needed and Safari/older browsers get smooth interpolation, (c) on burst:true, spawns 14 fixed-position 6px spans at the button's center and tweens each with physics2D:{ velocity:gsap.utils.random(260,420), angle:gsap.utils.random(-110,-70), gravity:900, friction:0.06 }, removed onComplete. Wiring per button: LikeButton already has buttonRef + useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef }); add the pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, '#ff3860', true) call inside the existing onClick toggle. SaveButton + ShareButton: add `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, attach `ref={buttonRef}`, wrap effects with `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, and call pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--gold)', false) [Save] / pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--text-muted)', false) [Share]. **--text-muted is already defined in frontend/app/globals.css at line 144 — no new color token, no globals.css change.** QuoteShare integration (chosen approach): WIDEN the signature in frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx line 170 from `onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number)` to `onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number, e?: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>)` and at line 217 change the onClick to `onClick={(e) => void onShareClick(target, i, e)}`. Inside onShareClick, if `e?.currentTarget` is present, call pressFeedback(e.currentTarget, 'var(--gold)', false). Rejected the ref-per-button alternative (an array of refs synced to the share targets array adds churn that the event-arg path avoids). Register Physics2DPlugin, CustomBounce, CustomEase in frontend/lib/gsap.ts.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Add tactile, physics-based click feedback to every primary action button: Like, Save, Share, and each per-target button inside QuoteShare. CustomBounce on the scale, box-shadow flash, optional Physics2D confetti burst on Like.

## Approach (committed decisions)

**Flash color mechanism — direct box-shadow tween** (NOT a CSS custom property). GSAP can interpolate `box-shadow` strings directly, so we sidestep needing `@property --pulse-flash` in globals.css and we get correct interpolation on older Safari.

**Per-button refs + useGSAP scope** — explicitly required for ALL three buttons, not just LikeButton (LikeButton already has it at line 17/44):
- `SaveButton.tsx`: add `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, attach `ref={buttonRef}`, wrap with `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, call `pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--gold)', false)` in onClick
- `ShareButton.tsx`: same pattern with `pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--text-muted)', false)`

**ShareButton flash color = `var(--text-muted)`** (already defined in `frontend/app/globals.css:144`). globals.css is NOT in filesToChange — no new color token needed.

**QuoteShare integration — widen the onClick signature** (NOT ref-per-button). Current state, verified:
- `frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx:170` is `const onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number) => { ... }` — no event arg
- `frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx:217` is `onClick={() => void onShareClick(target, i)}`

Change to:
- `const onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number, e?: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => { ... }`
- `onClick={(e) => void onShareClick(target, i, e)}`
- Inside the handler, when `e?.currentTarget` exists, call `pressFeedback(e.currentTarget, 'var(--gold)', false)`.

Rejected alternative: an array of refs synced to the targets array. The event-arg path is shorter and matches the existing pattern in the file.

## Files
- New: `frontend/lib/pressFeedback.ts`
- Modified: `LikeButton.tsx`, `SaveButton.tsx`, `ShareButton.tsx`, `QuoteShare.tsx` and their module.css siblings (only if a `transform-origin` tweak is needed)
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` — register Physics2DPlugin + CustomBounce + CustomEase

## Tuning
- CustomBounce: `strength: 0.55, squash: 1.4, endAtStart: false`
- Scale fromTo: `0.86 → 1` over 0.9s ease 'btnBounce'
- Box-shadow flash: 0→12px outset, 0.55s, color = `flashColor` then alpha 0
- Like burst: 14 particles, velocity 260-420, angle -110..-70, gravity 900, friction 0.06

## Reduced motion
When `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, pressFeedback skips the bounce + burst entirely and instead tweens box-shadow to a steady 0.85 alpha for 120ms then back. Color feedback remains, motion does not.

## Test plan
- [ ] Tap Like — squish + rebound, confetti burst, button settles
- [ ] Tap Save — squish + rebound, gold box-shadow flash, no particles
- [ ] Tap Share — squish + rebound, muted box-shadow flash, no particles
- [ ] Open QuoteShare, tap each share target — squish + gold flash per button
- [ ] Keyboard activate (Space/Enter) on each — same feedback (event still has currentTarget)
- [ ] Rapid double-tap — second tween overwrites first (overwrite:'auto'), no stacking
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — only the steady box-shadow pulse fires; no bounce/burst/squish
- [ ] Verify Physics2DPlugin loads in free GSAP — `gsap.registerPlugin` does not throw
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: pressFeedback's first line checks prefersReducedMotion(). When true: skip CustomBounce, skip particles, just gsap.fromTo(el, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 0 ${flashColor}` }, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 6px ${flashColor}00`, duration: 0.12 }). Color feedback remains.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Swapped the elastic/back.out ease for the physics-based-effects demo (CustomBounce + Physics2DPlugin). Dropped the CSS custom-property pulse trick in favor of tweening box-shadow directly — no @property registration in globals.css needed. Confirmed by reading frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx that onShareClick (line 170) takes (target, index) with NO event; committed to widening the signature and adding e?.currentTarget rather than the ref-array alternative. Made the useRef + useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef }) setup explicit for SaveButton AND ShareButton (LikeButton already has it). Pinned ShareButton's flash to `var(--text-muted)` (defined at globals.css:144) so globals.css is NOT in filesToChange.

tasks.title: Smooth scroll restore using ScrollToPlugin in useReadingPosition
tasks.useCase: When a returning visitor reopens a chapter they've already started, the page glides them back to their saved scroll position instead of jumping. Driven by a swap at frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts line 119 from `window.scrollTo({ top, behavior: 'instant' })` to a GSAP ScrollToPlugin tween, with auto-kill so any user input instantly cancels the restore.
tasks.approach: Register ScrollToPlugin in frontend/lib/gsap.ts alongside existing ScrollTrigger (single call: `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ScrollToPlugin)`). In useReadingPosition.ts, replace the `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` at line 119 with a branch: if `window.location.hash` is non-empty (especially `#:~:text=` text-fragment links) OR `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, KEEP the instant jump (hash precedence rule). Otherwise run `gsap.to(window, { scrollTo: { y: target, autoKill: true }, duration: 1.1, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto', onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update(), onAutoKill: () => { restoringRef.current = false }, onComplete: () => { restoringRef.current = false }, onInterrupt: () => { restoringRef.current = false } })`. Tween storage: add `const tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` in the hook; assign the tween to tweenRef.current and call tweenRef.current?.kill() in the existing cleanup return. Pause the write throttler during restore: add `const restoringRef = useRef(false)`, set it `true` immediately before launching the tween (and on the synchronous instant-jump branch too, for parity); inside onScroll, early-return `if (restoringRef.current) return;` so the programmatic scroll never triggers PATCHes. autoKill clears restoringRef via the three callbacks. Duration/ease pinned: 1.1s power2.out (no distance-aware scaling).
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Replace the instant `window.scrollTo` at `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts:119` with a GSAP `ScrollToPlugin` tween so returning readers glide back to their saved position.

## Decisions (committed)
- **Duration**: 1.1s fixed, no distance-aware scaling
- **Ease**: `power2.out`
- **autoKill**: `true` (default for window targets — any user wheel/touch/key input cancels the tween instantly, which is the whole point)
- **Hash precedence**: ANY non-empty `window.location.hash` — especially text fragments like `#:~:text=...` — wins; skip the tween and let the browser handle the anchor/fragment
- **Reduced motion**: skip the tween, retain the existing `behavior: 'instant'` scrollTo
- **Tween storage**: `const tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` so the existing cleanup return can `tweenRef.current?.kill()`
- **ScrollTrigger coordination**: pass `onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update()` so any ScrollTrigger-driven reveals on the page fire correctly during the programmatic scroll
- **Write-throttle pause**: `const restoringRef = useRef(false)`; set true immediately before launching the tween; in `onScroll`, early-return when true; clear via `onAutoKill | onComplete | onInterrupt`. Prevents 100+ wasted PATCH calls during the 1.1s tween (the existing `WRITE_THROTTLE_MS = 5000` only kicks in after the first write)

## Files
- `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts` (line 119 + surrounding effect)
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (register ScrollToPlugin)

## Test plan
- [ ] Reopen /chapter/[id] mid-article — scroll glides to saved position in 1.1s with power2.out
- [ ] Flick the wheel mid-restore — tween aborts instantly (autoKill)
- [ ] Hit PageDown mid-restore — tween aborts (autoKill catches keyboard too)
- [ ] Open /chapter/[id]#some-heading — instant anchor jump, no tween
- [ ] Open /chapter/[id]#:~:text=hello — instant text-fragment scroll, no tween
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — instant restore, no tween
- [ ] Network tab — exactly 0 PATCH /reading-positions calls fired during the 1.1s tween (proves restoringRef guard)
- [ ] Unmount mid-tween (route change) — no console errors; tween cleaned via tweenRef.current?.kill()
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: If `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, retain the existing `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` branch unchanged. Animating ~1s of vertical scroll is a known vestibular trigger; the instant jump is the correct fallback. Note that even without reduce-motion, autoKill makes the tween instantly yield to any user keyboard/wheel/touch input, which is itself an a11y win.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Pinned `tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` so cleanup can kill the tween (matches existing cleanup return at line 202-214). Added `onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update()` so ScrollTrigger reveals fire during the programmatic scroll. Added the `restoringRef` write-throttle pause so the tween itself doesn't trigger writes inside `onScroll` (the throttler doesn't otherwise gate the first write of a session). Pinned duration 1.1s + ease `power2.out` (no distance-aware variant). Committed to ANY non-empty `window.location.hash` (including `#:~:text=`) winning over the saved-position restore.

tasks.title: FLIP-based tag filter reflow on /search and /browse
tasks.useCase: Clicking a tag in TagBar on /search or /browse reflows the result grid with GSAP Flip so cards slide from their old slots to their new slots (and leavers fade out absolute-positioned without shoving siblings). Today the navigation full-replaces the card list with no animation.
tasks.approach: Because /search and /browse are server components that re-render the CardGrid on every URL change, the demo's pattern (Flip.getState before mutation, Flip.from after) does NOT survive across navigation — node refs are gone. Committed solution: a module-level FlipBridge in frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts that stashes a serialized Flip state keyed by the pathname + previous tagIds. TagBar's click handler (intercepted) calls bridge.snapshot(gsap.utils.toArray('[data-flip-id]')) synchronously before router.push, storing `Flip.getState(items, { props: 'opacity,transform' })` (state objects survive across renders because they hold cloned rects, not live nodes). On the next render, CardGrid mounts inside a useGSAP that pulls bridge.consume() and calls `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.out', absolute: true, simple: true, stagger: { amount: 0.4 }, onEnter: els => gsap.fromTo(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.4 }), onLeave: els => gsap.to(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.3 }) })`. Suspense boundary: because the new client CardGrid reads useSearchParams, wrap CardGrid uses in `<Suspense fallback={<CardGrid.Skeleton />}>` inside frontend/app/search/page.tsx and frontend/app/browse/page.tsx. Card identity: every card carries `data-flip-id={`${type}:${id}`}` — added to StoryCard, SeriesCard, ContinueCard. ContinueCard.tsx and ContinueReadingRow.tsx are in scope because /search results can include continue-reading cards. Grid min-height: pin `min-height` on the .grid container at the start of Flip.from via a `gsap.set(container, { minHeight: container.offsetHeight })` and clear it onComplete — prevents the parent shrinking when leavers go absolute. Fast-Refresh safety: in flipBridge.ts add `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (module as any).hot) { (module as any).hot.dispose(() => bridge.clear()); }` plus an exported `bridge.clear()` callable. Document in a code comment that this is Webpack HMR API; the Next.js equivalent for Turbopack is `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose?.(() => bridge.clear())`. Feature flag: gate the entire client CardGrid behavior on `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER === '1'` — when off, fall back to the existing server-render path so a regression can ship dark. /tag/[slug] is OUT of scope (it's a separate route segment; the flipBridge does not span across route segment changes cleanly because both the page shell and the grid unmount).
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
GSAP Flip-based reflow on /search and /browse when the tag filter changes — cards slide from old slot to new slot, leavers fade out absolutely, enterers fade+scale in.

## Why
Demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/flexbox-filtering/ — but the demo runs entirely client-side. Our /search and /browse are server components, so the verbatim pattern can't survive a `router.push`.

## Architecture (committed)

**Module-level FlipBridge** (`frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts`):
- `snapshot(items)` → stores `Flip.getState(items, { props: 'opacity,transform' })` plus a key (pathname + prev tagIds)
- `consume()` → returns the state and clears it (one-shot)
- `clear()` → for HMR / Fast Refresh
- Flip states hold cloned rects, not live node refs, so they survive the unmount/remount across navigation

**Suspense**: CardGrid becomes a client component that reads `useSearchParams`. Wrap its callsites with `<Suspense fallback={<CardGrid.Skeleton />}>` in `frontend/app/search/page.tsx` and `frontend/app/browse/page.tsx` (Next.js requirement when calling `useSearchParams` in a child of a server page).

**Card identity**: every card root carries `data-flip-id={`${type}:${id}`}` so Flip can match across the navigation. Required on StoryCard, SeriesCard, ContinueCard.

**ContinueCard / ContinueReadingRow** are in scope — `/search` results can include continue-reading rows and they also need `data-flip-id`.

**Flip options** (committed):
```
Flip.from(state, {
  duration: 0.55,
  ease: 'power2.out',
  absolute: true,    // leavers go position:absolute so survivors don't fight reflow
  simple: true,      // skip nested-element diffing — flat list of cards, faster
  stagger: { amount: 0.4 },  // total stagger budget, not per-item (handles 50+ cards)
  onEnter: els => gsap.fromTo(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.4 }),
  onLeave: els => gsap.to(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.3 }),
})
```

**Grid stability**: pin `gsap.set(container, { minHeight: container.offsetHeight })` at the start of the Flip and clear it `onComplete` so the parent doesn't shrink when leavers go absolute.

**Fast Refresh / HMR**: in `flipBridge.ts`,
```
if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (module as any).hot) {
  (module as any).hot.dispose(() => bridge.clear());
}
```
Document in code comment that this is the legacy Webpack HMR API; under Turbopack use `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose?.(() => bridge.clear())`.

**Feature flag**: gate the whole client-side CardGrid behavior behind `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER === '1'`. T5 has the most production risk, so it ships dark and is toggled per-environment.

## Out of scope
- `/tag/[slug]` — separate route segment, page shell unmounts, the flipBridge does not span it cleanly
- Reading-position carryover on the cards (unrelated)

## Cross-cutting note (read T4 first)
`frontend/lib/gsap.ts` needs to register Flip. Whichever of T4 / T5 lands first must consolidate plugin registration into one call: `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ScrollToPlugin, Flip)`.

## Test plan
- [ ] /search, click a tag — cards reflow with Flip, no full-page navigation flash
- [ ] /browse, click a tag — same
- [ ] Click a tag that leaves only 2 results — leavers fade absolute, survivors slide to new flex slots
- [ ] Click All — all cards re-enter with onEnter fade+scale
- [ ] 50+ cards visible — total stagger stays under 0.5s (proves stagger.amount budget)
- [ ] Turn off `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER` — falls back to existing server-render, no animation, no regression
- [ ] Hit /tag/[slug] from /search — full navigation, no Flip attempt (confirms out-of-scope)
- [ ] Trigger a Fast Refresh while a tag filter is mid-animation — no orphan bridge state, no Flip-on-stale-nodes error
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — Flip.from is replaced with `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0 })` so positions sync without animation
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: When `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, CardGrid still consumes the bridge state but calls `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0 })` so the layout syncs instantly with no transition — onEnter/onLeave become synchronous opacity sets. Stagger.amount drops to 0. The min-height pin happens but clears synchronously.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Committed to the module-level flipBridge architecture (instead of leaving the choice between bridge/intercept-then-navigate/client-only-filter open). Explicitly added Suspense to filesToChange via frontend/app/search/page.tsx and frontend/app/browse/page.tsx — required because the new client CardGrid reads useSearchParams. Pinned `{ absolute: true, simple: true }` on Flip.from and added the grid container min-height pin. Added the Fast-Refresh-safe `bridge.clear()` via Webpack HMR `module.hot.dispose` with a code comment about the Turbopack equivalent. Added ContinueCard.tsx + ContinueReadingRow.tsx + StoryCard.tsx + SeriesCard.tsx to filesToChange because they all need `data-flip-id`. Marked /tag/[slug] explicitly out of scope. Added the `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER` env-var feature flag for T5 only (other tasks ship without a flag).

suggestedSequence.rationale: Ship smooth scroll restore first — smallest blast radius (one hook, one line replaced) and it touches frontend/lib/gsap.ts. Whichever of T4/T5 lands first MUST collapse plugin registration into a single `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ...)` call rather than separate calls, because GSAP's registerPlugin accepts multiple args and a second call costs an unnecessary module evaluation.

Physics-based button feedback next — independent of T4, no cross-cutting plugin registration concerns beyond Physics2DPlugin/CustomBounce/CustomEase additions (multi-arg registerPlugin call established by T4). High user-visible win, low coupling.
Admin NoteCard Flip — adds Flip to the registerPlugin call. Lower production risk than T5 because admin-only. Validates the Flip integration before we expose it to public traffic in T5.

Magnetic dock — depends on the CSS hover-transform removals being correct, and benefits from being applied AFTER T2 sets the overwrite:'auto' pattern that lets multiple GSAP writers share a transform. Touches the most React components (hero, CardGrid, ContinueReadingRow, ChapterList) but no new plugin registration.

Ship last — feature-flagged behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER`. Highest risk (server→client conversion of CardGrid, Suspense additions, flipBridge module-state). By landing after T1, the cards already have stable refs and overwrite:'auto' on transform writes; the Flip reflow won't fight the dock hover.

openQuestions: Particle z-index for T3's Like burst: should the spans render fixed-position z:9999 over the entire viewport (current spec), or be appended inside the LikeButton wrapper so they're clipped by overflow:hidden on the reading view? The wrapper approach is safer for stacked modals but eats the burst on small buttons.

T5 stagger budget: 0.4s total feels right at 30+ cards, but on a sparse /search result (3 cards) a 0.4 budget means 0.13s per card and reads as too snappy. Should the stagger be a function like `{ each: 0.08, from: 'start', amount: undefined }` clamped at 0.4 max, or stay as a fixed `amount: 0.4` and accept the snappy small-set feel?

T2 autosave-on-collapsed-card guard: should a collapsed card's textarea ALSO save on blur (the current behavior — guard only blocks the always-mounted-but-collapsed branch's debounce timer), or does blur-save on collapsed cards need an explicit `if (expanded)` block too?

gaps: T1 SeriesCard does NOT have its own SeriesCard.module.css — it imports from StoryCard.module.css (verified at /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/components/SeriesCard.tsx line 9). The plan's reference to 'SeriesCard CSS' in T1's filesToChange is fictitious; the actual file is StoryCard.module.css and the same .card:hover rule there affects both StoryCard and SeriesCard. The plan needs to be explicit that there is a SHARED CSS module.

T1 plan does not address the conflict with CardGrid's existing gsap.from entrance reveal at /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/components/CardGrid.tsx lines 16-37. That entrance writes y/opacity on the same elements that useMagneticDock will write to on pointermove. Even with overwrite:auto, racing the entrance reveal with a hover during stagger will look chaotic. Plan must specify dock listeners attach only after the entrance reveal completes (e.g., onComplete callback) or that the dock listener only activates after window 'load' / first idle.

T1 ContinueReadingRow card hover rule cleanup is specified but ContinueCard.module.css (used by ResumeReadingRow on /browse) is NOT in T1's filesToChange — ContinueCard is the per-item card whereas ContinueReadingRow is the localStorage-backed homepage row. The plan conflates them. ContinueCard.module.css needs the same transform-on-hover removal.

T1 mentions 'StoryCard.module.css' for cleanup but the actual hover/transform rule needs to be inspected — the plan never reads the file to confirm a .card:hover transform exists there. If it does, both .card:hover (StoryCard/SeriesCard share this file) AND the entrance reveal need coordination.

T1 does not address the existence of data-tag-ids already on the Link roots of SeriesCard/StoryCard at SeriesCard.tsx:43, 94 and StoryCard.tsx:31. The plan should call out that data-dock-item and data-tag-ids must both live on the same node and data-flip-id (from T5) too — and how to keep them distinct.

T2 NoteCard.module.css has @keyframes noteExpandIn at lines 109-118 plus 'animation: noteExpandIn 200ms ...' on .expanded at line 106. This CSS animation runs every time the expanded class lands and WILL collide with Flip.from's transform writes — Flip.from animates transform, the CSS animation also animates transform via translateY(-3px → 0). Plan does not list this rule for removal.

T2 NoteCard.module.css .collapsed:hover at lines 42-45 sets transform: translateY(-1px) — that transform-on-hover will fight the T1 magnetic-dock writes if note cards ever participate in dock. Plan only mentions removing the .card transition-transform leg at lines 18-22 but leaves the explicit :hover transform on .collapsed.

T2 NotesPanel.module.css already has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block at lines 242-252 setting 'transition: none !important'. Removing 'max-height 260ms ...' from the panel transition for Flip is fine, but the reduced-motion override is already in place. Plan does not reconcile that the reduce-motion path inherits transition:none and Flip.from is skipped → the panel resize when expanded happens via the synchronous CSS class swap, which is correct, but the .panel.hasExpanded ALSO sets min-height/max-height as hard layout numbers (lines 43-44) so the layout still snaps. Plan misses this.

T2 'always render both branches' contradicts current NoteCard.tsx structure — the function returns two completely different JSX trees at lines 174-191 (pill) vs 194-229 (expanded). To always render both, NoteCard must be rewritten to render BOTH subtrees and toggle visibility/opacity. The plan's autosave guard is moot because if both are rendered, the textarea is always in the DOM, and the existing useEffect-debounces at lines 76-95 fire on title/body state changes regardless of expanded. The 'check expanded synchronously inside the autosave handler' guard would need to gate the onChange callback inside the useEffect, not block input handlers. Plan does not specify the refactor scope.

T2 Flip.getState() must be called BEFORE the React commit phase. The plan says 'in the click handler immediately before the React state update' which is correct, but on a parent (NotesPanel) calling setState. To make Flip work cleanly, the cleanest pattern is useLayoutEffect with a previousId ref to compare against current — capture state in the layout effect's cleanup of the previous render and trigger Flip.from in the next layout effect. Plan does not specify the actual capture mechanics.

T3 ShareButton.tsx currently has NO useGSAP, useRef on the button, or gsap import. Adding 'const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)' alone isn't enough — the plan needs to import gsap, useGSAP, prefersReducedMotion from '@/lib/gsap' and add a useGSAP scope wrapper. Plan mentions this but does not list it in 'files modified' shape — the import set changes for ShareButton + SaveButton.

T3 SaveButton has TWO render branches: unauthenticated returns a <Link> (lines 58-69), authenticated returns a <button> (lines 96-108). The plan does not specify pressFeedback only attaches to the authenticated branch and not the link.

T3 GSAP free-tier claim: the plan says 'Physics2DPlugin + CustomBounce + CustomEase (all in GSAP free tier as of GSAP 3.13+; verify isPaidPlugin:false at time of implementation)'. The installed version per /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/node_modules/gsap/package.json is 3.15.0 which DOES include those plugins (Physics2DPlugin.js, CustomBounce.js, CustomEase.js are physically present in node_modules/gsap/). Plan's hedge is unnecessary BUT the plan never confirms via filesystem check — which it should.

T3 box-shadow tweening: GSAP can interpolate numeric values within box-shadow strings, but if .button has a :hover box-shadow set in CSS, the next paint after the tween settles will overwrite the GSAP-set value with the :hover one. Plan does not call out the need to inspect each button's existing :hover box-shadow rule (LikeButton.module.css, SaveButton.module.css, ShareButton.module.css, QuoteShare.module.css) and decide on overrides.

T3 'Color feedback remains' for reduced motion via box-shadow fromTo with 0.12s — but a 0.12s box-shadow tween IS motion (animated alpha/spread). For true reduced-motion compliance, the color flash should also be skipped, OR the plan should use a non-animated class toggle.

T3 Per-button refs in QuoteShare: the plan correctly chooses the event.currentTarget path. But the existing onClick at /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx:217 is `onClick={() => void onShareClick(target, i)}` — when the user invokes via keyboard Space/Enter, the event still has currentTarget. Plan is correct but should pin the React.MouseEvent vs React.KeyboardEvent typing — currentTarget exists on both but the type signature is React.SyntheticEvent if both are accepted.

T4 The cleanup return at /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts lines 202-214 already calls flushPending() which fires sendNow() — combined with restoringRef.current being true at unmount-time would early-return the write. Plan must clarify that the cleanup ALSO needs to set restoringRef.current = false before flushPending() so the final write goes through.

T4 'restoringRef' guard: setting restoringRef.current = true before the tween fires but the tween itself is non-blocking (gsap.to is async). The 'before launching' assignment is fine for scroll events fired by the tween, but the FIRST scroll event after the tween starts might race the synchronous set if the tween's first ScrollTrigger.update() fires before the ref is set. Plan should specify: set restoringRef BEFORE constructing the tween config.

T4 The hash-precedence rule says 'KEEP the instant jump' when window.location.hash is non-empty. But the existing code at line 119 is window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' }) — note that `behavior: 'instant'` is the explicit non-smooth value. The browser anchor jump for hashes happens at navigation time, not at this hook's restore step. So when a hash is present, the hook should SKIP the restore entirely (let the browser handle the anchor) rather than 'keep the instant jump' (which would override the anchor). Plan conflates these two semantics.

T4 'duration: 1.1, ease: power2.out' is a fixed-distance tween. For a 200vh-tall chapter, 1.1s feels right; for a 10000vh-tall novel chapter, 1.1s scrolls past content too fast for the reader to register where they landed. Plan rejects distance-aware scaling but should at least specify a min-distance threshold below which the tween is skipped (e.g., target < 200px → instant jump).

T5 CardGrid currently is a client component that runs an entrance-reveal gsap.from on scroll (lines 23-37). Replacing or augmenting this with Flip.from for tag-filter reflows means the entrance reveal needs to be conditionally suppressed when consume() returns a state (i.e., the user arrived via a tag click, not first visit). Plan does not describe how to gate entrance reveal vs Flip reflow.

T5 The plan references `<CardGrid.Skeleton />` as a Suspense fallback — CardGrid is a default function export and has no static .Skeleton property. This is a fabricated API. Plan needs to specify creating a separate skeleton component (e.g., CardGridSkeleton in frontend/components/CardGridSkeleton.tsx).

T5 TagBar uses Next.js <Link> elements for pill navigation (TagBar.tsx lines 151-156 'All' link, line 165 Pill->Link via buildTagHref). Snapshotting Flip state BEFORE router.push requires intercepting the Link click via onClick with e.preventDefault() + router.push, OR replacing Link with button. The plan glosses over this with 'TagBar click handler (intercepted)' but the actual click is handled by Link itself. This is a real refactor that needs to be enumerated.

T5 CardGrid is a wrapper that accepts children — it has no knowledge of the tagIds keyed in the bridge snapshot. Where does CardGrid read the tagIds to know which snapshot to consume? The plan says 'on the next render, CardGrid mounts inside a useGSAP that pulls bridge.consume()' — but consume() needs a key match. CardGrid currently doesn't read URL params. The plan needs to specify either (a) pass tagIds as a prop, or (b) read useSearchParams inside CardGrid (which forces every parent of CardGrid into a Suspense boundary).

T5 Suspense scope: the plan places Suspense around CardGrid callsites in /search and /browse, but useSearchParams must be wrapped by Suspense at any client tree that reads it. If CardGrid now reads useSearchParams, the Suspense must encompass not just the CardGrid block but anything that streams below it. Plan is too narrow — the recommended boundary is the entire `<main>` block, not the individual CardGrid invocations.

T5 Fast-Refresh / HMR snippet uses `(module as any).hot.dispose(...)` (Webpack HMR API). Next.js 16 (per package.json `next: ^16.2.6`) uses Turbopack in dev by default. Plan acknowledges Turbopack equivalent but the chosen primary path is the Webpack API. The plan should make Turbopack the primary path: `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (import.meta as any).webpackHot) { (import.meta as any).webpackHot.dispose(() => bridge.clear()); }`. Also frontend/AGENTS.md explicitly warns 'This is NOT the Next.js you know — read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing any code'. Plan ignores this warning.

T5 ContinueCard and ContinueReadingRow are listed in T5 filesToChange but ContinueCard is NOT a card type that appears in CardGrid on /search — it appears in the ResumeReadingRow row on /browse only. Including it in T5 is over-scoped — the tag-filter reflow doesn't touch the ResumeReadingRow at all. Plan should remove ContinueCard.tsx and ContinueReadingRow.tsx from T5.

T5 data-flip-id collision: SeriesCard and StoryCard already carry data-tag-ids on their <Link>. Adding data-flip-id is fine syntactically but the plan should pin that data-flip-id includes a stable id (e.g., `series:${id}` vs `story:${id}` vs `chapter:${id}`) to disambiguate when /search shows both Stories and Series sections (page.tsx lines 92-115 — they're TWO separate CardGrids, not one). With two separate CardGrids and two separate flipBridge snapshots, the bridge needs to key per-CardGrid not per-page. Plan ignores this.

T5 NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER feature flag: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build time, not toggleable per-request. Shipping dark means a new build is required to toggle. Plan presents this as 'toggled per-environment' which is correct but does not address that there's no runtime override.

T2 estimatedPRs: 1, T5 estimatedPRs: 2 — but T5's plan describes a single feature-flagged ship behind one env var, plus the CardGrid client conversion + flipBridge + Suspense changes. Two PRs is reasonable but the plan does not split which work goes into which PR (e.g., 'PR1: convert CardGrid to client + Suspense; PR2: add flipBridge + TagBar intercept').

T3 and T4 both modify frontend/lib/gsap.ts. Sequencing note exists ('whichever of T4/T5 lands first must consolidate plugin registration into one call') but T3 ALSO registers plugins (Physics2DPlugin, CustomBounce, CustomEase). The cross-cutting consolidation rule must cover T3 too — currently the plan only mentions T4/T5.
T1 estimatedPRs: 1 but T1 touches 9 files + creates 2 — that's a sizable single PR. The plan does not flag risk of splitting (e.g., hook + CSS cleanup PR, then per-component data-dock-item PR).

T1 The hook 'no-ops the listener entirely' on reduced motion — but T1 ALSO removes CSS :hover transforms. Reduced-motion users will have NEITHER the dock effect NOR the original CSS hover lift. Plan acknowledges this in reducedMotionPlan ('a strictly static row with no transform on hover') but does not flag that this is a UX regression for that audience — they previously had a 2px lift, now they have nothing.

T1 Touch / mobile: pointermove is fired by touch on iOS Safari but with very different cadence. Magnetic dock effects typically feel wrong on touch (cursor-less). Plan does not specify a media query / pointer:fine gate to disable the hook on touch devices.
strongPoints: T3 correctly identifies QuoteShare.tsx line 170 onShareClick signature and line 217 onClick wiring — verified accurate against source code. Choosing the event-arg widening over a ref-array is the cleaner path.
T3 correctly identifies --text-muted as defined at frontend/app/globals.css:144 — verified.
T1 correctly identifies frontend/app/page.tsx as a server component exporting metadata, requiring a client wrapper HeroCardsList.tsx to host pointermove. The architectural fix is correct.
T1 correctly identifies the ChapterList row as a <Link className={styles.row}> at /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx line 82-84 — verified.
T1 correctly identifies ContinueReadingRow.module.css lines 63-70 with the transform-transition + hover-transform rules to remove — verified line-accurate against the file.
T4 correctly identifies useReadingPosition.ts line 119 as the single replacement point — verified.
T4's autoKill + restoringRef pattern to suppress writes during programmatic scroll is the correct architecture. The onUpdate: ScrollTrigger.update() is a real concern that's properly addressed.
T4's hash-precedence rule for #:~:text= text fragments is a real consideration — modern browsers handle these natively and a tween would race the browser's own scroll.
T2 correctly identifies the need to register Flip in gsap.ts and acknowledges the cross-cutting plugin consolidation with T4/T5.
T5's module-level FlipBridge architecture (snapshot before router.push, consume on next render) is the only viable way to do Flip across Next.js navigations — server components don't preserve refs.
T5's `{ absolute: true, simple: true }` Flip options + grid container min-height pin are the correct mitigations for leavers shoving the parent's height. The reasoning is sound.
T5's NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER feature flag is appropriate for the highest-risk task.

All plugins required (Flip, ScrollToPlugin, Physics2DPlugin, CustomBounce, CustomEase) physically exist in /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/frontend/node_modules/gsap/ at version 3.15.0 — no install step required.

Use a useLayoutEffect-based snapshot pattern: in NotesPanel, useRef the previous expandedId, when it changes call Flip.getState() in a useLayoutEffect on .card descendants BEFORE the new branch renders, then call Flip.from in the next layout effect. This avoids the textarea-in-DOM-while-collapsed problem entirely.
